source_text: Ἔρχεται καὶ δι' ὀλίγους ἐπὶ δῆμον κακὰ, καὶ μοχθηρίας τινὸς παραπήλαυσε δῆμος. Ἄχαρ ἱεροσύλησε, καὶ ὅλη ἡ παράταξις ἐμαστίζετο. Ὁ Ζαμβρὶ πάλιν εἰς τὰς Μαδιανίτιδας ἐξεπόρνευσε, καὶ ὁ Ἰσραὴλ ἔπιπτεν εἰς δίκην. Πάντες τοίνυν καὶ ἰδίᾳ καὶ κοινῇ τοὺς βίους ἑαυ τῶν ἐξετάσωμεν, ὡς παιδαγωγῷ πρόσχωμεν τῷ αὐχμῷ, ἕκαστον τῆς ἰδίας ἁμαρτίας ὑπομιμνήσκοντι. Εἴπωμεν καὶ ἡμεῖς τοῦ γενναίου Ἰὼβ τὴν φωνὴν εὐαισθήτως· Χεὶρ Κυρίου ἐστὶν, ἡ ἁψαμένη μου. Καὶ μάλιστα μὲν πρωτοτύπως τοῖς ἁμαρτήμασι τὴν συμφορὰν ἑαυτῶν λογισώμεθα. Εἰ δὲ δεῖ καὶ ἄλλο προσθεῖναι, ἔστιν ὅτε καὶ κατὰ πεῖραν ταῖς ψυχαῖς αἱ τοιαῦται τοῦ βίου δυσκληρίαι τοῖς ἀνθρώποις προσ άγονται, ἵν' ἐπὶ τῆς δυσκολίας ἀπελεγχθῶσιν οἱ δόκι μοι, εἴτε πένητες εἴτε πλούσιοι· ἑκάτεροι γὰρ ἀκρι βῶς διὰ τῆς ὑπομονῆς δοκιμάζονται. Κἀν τούτῳ μάλιστα τῷ καιρῷ διαδείκνυνται ὁ μὲν, εἰ κοινωνικὸς καὶ φιλάδελφος, ὁ δὲ, εἰ εὐχάριστος καὶ μὴ τοὐναντίον βλάσφημος, ταῖς τοῦ βίου περιφοραῖς ὀξέως συμμεταβάλλων τὸ φρόνημα. Οἶδα ἐγὼ πολλοὺς (οὐκ ἀκοῇ μαθὼν, ἀλλὰ τῇ πείρᾳ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους γνωρί σας), ἕως μέχρι μὲν ὁ βίος αὐτοῖς πρὸς εὐπορίαν διαμετρεῖται, καὶ ἐξ οὐρίας, τὸ λεγόμενον, χωρεῖ, μέσως γοῦν, εἰ καὶ μὴ τελείως, τῷ εὐεργέτῃ ὁμολογοῦντας τὴν χάριν· εἰ δέ που διὰ τὴν ἐναντίαν κατάστασιν περιτραπείη τὰ πράγματα, καὶ ὁ μὲν πλού σιος γένηται πένης, ἡ δὲ ῥώμη τοῦ σώματος νόσος, ἡ δὲ δόξα καὶ περιφάνεια αἰσχύνη καὶ ἀτιμία, ἀχαριστοῦντας, βλάσφημα φθεγγομένους, ὀκνοῦντας τὴν προσευχήν· ὡς πρὸς χρεώστην βραδύνοντα τὸν Θεὸν σχετλιάζοντας, οὐχ ὡς πρὸς Δεσπότην ἀγανακτοῦντα διακειμένους . Ἀλλ' ἄπαγε τῶν λογισμῶν τὴν τοιαύ την ἔννοιαν! Ὅταν δὲ ἴδῃς Θεὸν μὴ χαριζόμενον τὰ συνήθη, οὕτω λογίζου παρὰ σεαυτῷ· Μὴ ἀδύνατος ὁ Θεὸς χορηγεῖν τὴν τροφήν; Καὶ πῶς; ὅς γε Κύριός ἐστιν οὐρανοῦ καὶ πάσης διακοσμήσεως, ὡρῶν καὶ καιρῶν σοφὸς οἰκονόμος, κυβερνήτης τῶν πάντων, ὥσπερ τινὰ χορὸν εὔτακτον τὰς ὥρας καὶ τὰς τροπὰς ἀλλήλαις ὑποχωρεῖν ὁρίσας, ἵνα τῇ ἑαυτῶν ποικιλίᾳ ταῖς διαφόροις ἡμῶν ἐπαρκέσωσι χρείαις· καὶ νῦν μὲν κατὰ καιρὸν τὸ ὑγρὸν προσγένηται, αὖθις δὲ λάβῃ τὸ θερμὸν, καὶ τὸ ψυχρὸν ἐγκραθῇ τῷ ἐνιαυ τῷ, καὶ τοῦ ξηροῦ τὴν χρείαν μὴ ἀμοιρήσωμεν. Οὐκοῦν δυνατὸς ὁ Θεός· τοῦ δυνατοῦ δὲ προσόντος καὶ ὁμολογουμένου, μὴ ἆρα τὸ ἀγαθὸν ἐνέλειψεν; Οὐδὲ οὗτος ἐφεστὼς ὁ λόγος. Τίς γὰρ ἀνάγκη τὸν μὴ ἀγαθὸν ἔπεισεν ἐν ἀρχῇ δημιουργῆσαι τὸν ἄνθρωπον; Τίς δὲ ὁ κατεπείξας τὸν Κτίστην καὶ μὴ βουλόμενον χοῦν λαβεῖν, καὶ τοιοῦτον ἐκ πηλοῦ κάλ λος εἰδοποιῆσαι; Τίς ὁ πρὸς ἀνάγκην πείσας κατ' εἰκόνα ἰδίαν τὸν λόγον τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ χαρίσασθαι, ἵν' ἐκεῖθεν ὁρμηθεὶς τεχνῶν μάθησιν δέξηται, καὶ μάθῃ περὶ τῶν ἀνωτάτω φιλοσοφεῖν, ὧν αἰσθη τῶς οὐχ ἅπτεται; Κἂν, οὕτω λογιζόμενος, εὕρῃς τὴν ἀγαθότητα τῷ Θεῷ συνοῦσαν, καὶ μέχρι καὶ νῦν μὴ ἀπολιμπανομένην. Ἐπεὶ τί ἐκώλυεν, εἰπέ μοι, μὴ αὐχμὸν εἶναι τὸ ὁρώμενον, ἀλλὰ τελείαν ἐκπύρωσιν; καὶ μικρὸν ὑπαλλάξαντα τὸν ἥλιον τῆς συνήθους πορείας, πλησιάσαντα δὲ τοῖς περιγείοις σώμασιν, ἐν ἀκαρεῖ καταφλέξαι πᾶν τὸ ὁρώμενον; ἢ βρέξαι πῦρ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καθ' ὁμοίωσιν τῶν ἤδη κολάσεων τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν; Ἐπὶ σαυτοῦ καὶ τῶν σῶν λογισμῶν γενοῦ, ἄνθρωπε· μὴ ποίει τὰ τῶν ἀνοήτων παίδων, οἳ, παρὰ διδασκάλου ἐπιτιμηθέντες, τὰς δέλτους ἐκείνου καταῤῥηγνύουσι· πατρὸς δὲ, δι' ὠφέλειαν τὴν τροφὴν ὑπερθεμένου, τὴν ἐσθῆτα κατασπαράτ τουσιν, ἢ τὸ τῆς μητρὸς πρόσωπον τοῖς ὄνυξι κα ταξαίνουσι.
thought_title: Disaster as shared correction and test
orientation: Basil continues his homily, arguing that the drought is God's corrective punishment for the people's sins, especially their failure to share with the poor.
pass_a_gloss: Evils come also upon a people because of a few, and a people enjoyed the fruits of someone's wickedness. Achan committed sacrilege, and the whole army was scourged. Zimri again committed fornication with the Midianite women, and Israel fell into punishment. Let us all therefore examine our own lives both privately and in common, so that we may attend to the drought as to a tutor, reminding each one of his own sin. Let us also say the voice of the noble Job with feeling: The hand of the Lord is the one that touched me. And especially let us reckon the disaster to ourselves as primarily due to our sins. But if one must add another point, sometimes such hardships of life are brought upon human souls also as a test, so that in the difficulty the approved may be exposed, whether poor or rich; for both are tested precisely through endurance. And especially at this time are revealed the one, whether he is sharing and loving toward one another, and the other, whether he is thankful and not the opposite, a blasphemer, quickly changing his mind along with the turns of life. I know many (not having learned by hearsay, but having known the people by experience), as long as their life is measured out toward prosperity, and goes, as the saying is, with a fair wind, at least moderately, if not perfectly, acknowledging the favor to the benefactor; but if somewhere their affairs are turned around because of the opposite condition, and the rich man becomes poor, and the strength of the body becomes sickness, and the glory and distinction become shame and dishonor, they are ungrateful, uttering blasphemies, shrinking from prayer; complaining against God as against a debtor who is slow, not being disposed as toward a Master who is indignant. But away with such a thought from your reasonings! But whenever you see God not granting the usual things, reason thus with yourself: Is God unable to supply food? And how? He who is Lord of heaven and of all its ordering, a wise steward of hours and seasons, pilot of all things, having ordained that the hours and the turnings yield to one another like some well-ordered chorus, so that by their variety they may supply our different needs; and now in season the moisture may come, and again the heat may take its turn, and the cold may be mixed into the year, and we may not lack the use of the dry. Therefore God is able; and since the able is present and acknowledged, did the good then fail? Nor does this argument stand. For what necessity persuaded the one who is not good to create man in the beginning? And who pressed the Creator, even not willing, to take dust, and to form such beauty from clay? Who persuaded him under compulsion to grant the Word according to his own image to man, so that setting out from there he might receive the learning of arts, and might learn to philosophize about the highest things, which he does not touch by sense? And if, reasoning thus, you find that goodness is with God, and even until now has not departed. Since what prevented, tell me, the thing seen being not a drought, but a complete burning up? and the sun, having changed a little from its customary course, and having drawn near to the bodies around the earth, in an instant to burn up everything seen? or to rain fire from heaven, in the likeness of the punishments already of sinners? Come to yourself and to your own reasonings, man; do not do the things of foolish children, who, having been rebuked by a teacher, tear up his writing tablets; and of a father, who has postponed food for their benefit, they tear his clothing, or scratch the face of their mother with their nails.

choices.why: The verb παραπολαύω means to enjoy a share of something, often with a negative connotation of suffering consequences; 'enjoyed the fruits of' captures the sense that the people shared in the results of the wickedness.

choices.english: so that we may attend to the drought as to a tutor
choices.why: The παιδαγωγός is a tutor or guide who corrects; Basil frames the drought as a corrective instructor, so 'tutor' preserves the pedagogical force.
The adverb means 'in the first place' or 'primarily'; Basil is saying the disaster should first and foremost be reckoned as due to sins.
πεῖρα means trial or test; the glossary gives 'trial' for πειρασμός, and here the related noun πεῖρα carries the same sense of testing.
δόκιμος means tested and found genuine; 'the approved' captures the sense of those who pass the test.

choices.term: οὐχ ὡς πρὸς Δεσπότην ἀγανακτοῦντα διακειμένους
choices.english: not being disposed as toward a Master who is indignant
choices.why: The Greek says they are NOT disposed as toward a Master who is indignant; the negation applies to the whole disposition, and ἀγανακτοῦντα modifies Δεσπότην, meaning the Master is indignant. The previous attempt wrongly negated the indignation itself.
rejected: not being indignant toward him as toward a Master

bible_refs.note: Χεὶρ Κυρίου ἐστὶν, ἡ ἁψαμένη μου

pass_b_english: Evils also come upon a whole people because of a few, and a people suffers from someone's wickedness. Achan committed sacrilege, and the whole army was scourged. Zimri in turn committed fornication with the Midianite women, and Israel fell under punishment. Let us all therefore examine our lives, both privately and together, so that we may attend to the drought as to a tutor, reminding each of us of his own sin. Let us also say with feeling the words of the noble Job: “The hand of the Lord has touched me” (Job 19:21). And above all, let us reckon the disaster as primarily due to our own sins. But if we must add another point, such hardships of life are sometimes brought upon people as a test for their souls, so that in difficulty the approved may be proved, whether poor or rich; for both are tested precisely through endurance. And especially at this time it is revealed whether one is generous and loving toward others, or whether he is thankful and not, on the contrary, blasphemous, quickly changing his mind along with life's reversals. I know many people—not from hearsay, but from knowing them by experience—who, as long as their life is measured out toward prosperity and runs, as the saying goes, with a fair wind, at least moderately, if not perfectly, acknowledge the grace of their benefactor. But if their affairs are turned around by the opposite condition, and the rich man becomes poor, and bodily strength becomes sickness, and glory and distinction become shame and dishonor, then they are ungrateful, uttering blasphemies, shrinking from prayer; complaining against God as against a creditor who is slow, not as people should feel toward a Master who is angry. But away with such a thought from your minds! Whenever you see God not granting the usual things, reason thus within yourself: Is God unable to supply food? And how could that be? He is Lord of heaven and of all its order, a wise steward of hours and seasons, the pilot of all things, who has ordained that the hours and the turns of the year yield to one another like a well-ordered chorus, so that by their variety they may supply our different needs; and now in season the moisture comes, and again the heat takes its turn, and the cold is blended into the year, and we do not lack the service of the dry season. Therefore God is able. And since the able is present and acknowledged, has the good then failed? This argument does not stand either. For what necessity persuaded him who was not good to create man in the beginning? Who compelled the Creator, though unwilling, to take dust and fashion such beauty from clay? Who compelled him by necessity to grant the Word to man according to his own image, so that setting out from there he might receive the learning of arts, and learn to philosophize about the highest things, which he does not grasp by sense? And if you reason thus, you will find that goodness is with God, and even now has not departed. For tell me, what prevented what we see from being not a drought but a complete conflagration? What prevented him from slightly shifting the sun from its customary course, bringing it near to the bodies on earth, and in an instant burning up everything visible? Or from raining fire from heaven, in the likeness of the punishments already inflicted on sinners? Come to yourself and your own thoughts, man; do not act like foolish children, who, when rebuked by their teacher, tear up his tablets; and when their father delays their food for their benefit, they rip their clothing, or scratch their mother's face with their nails.

problems.quote: enjoys the fruits of someone's wickedness
problems.why: παραπήλαυσε means suffered/shared in, not enjoys; sense is negative
problems.fix: a people suffers from someone's wickedness

problems.quote: not being disposed as toward a Master who is indignant
problems.source_quote: οὐχ ὡς πρὸς Δεσπότην ἀγανακτοῦντα διακειμένους
problems.why: misread: they are indignant, not the Master; ἀγανακτοῦντα modifies the people
problems.fix: not being indignant as toward a Master
problems.ruling: ἀγανακτοῦντα is accusative agreeing with Δεσπότην; people are διακειμένους, disposed toward an indignant Master.

edits.old: enjoys the fruits of someone's wickedness
not being disposed as toward a Master who is indignant
edits.new: not being indignant as toward a Master

fixed: παραπήλαυσε means 'suffered/shared in' negatively, not 'enjoys'; changed to 'suffers from'.
ἀγανακτοῦντα modifies the people (they are indignant), not the Master; changed to 'not being indignant as toward a Master'.

problems.quote: not being indignant as toward a Master
problems.source_quote: οὐχ ὡς πρὸς Δεσπότην ἀγανακτοῦντα διακειμένους
problems.why: English 'not being indignant' misses that they ARE indignant, but in wrong way; source says they complain like to a debtor, not being indignant as toward a Master—i.e., they lack proper indignation toward God as Master.
problems.fix: not disposed to be indignant as toward a Master

problems.why: English 'even not willing' is ungrammatical and obscures meaning; source asks who compelled the Creator though unwilling—rhetorical question about compulsion.
English inverts logic: source asks 'who persuaded him by necessity/compulsion' (i.e., forced him), not 'who persuaded him under compulsion' (someone else compelled).

problems.source_quote: ἵν' ἐπὶ τῆς δυσκολίας ἀπελεγχθῶσιν οἱ δόκιμοι
problems.why: ἀπελεγχθῶσιν means 'proved/tested/shown'; 'exposed' implies discredited, reversing the sense.
problems.ruling: ἀπελεγχθῶσιν means 'tested/proved true', not 'exposed' in negative sense; 'exposed' misleads reader.

problems.quote: complaining against God as against a debtor who is slow
problems.source_quote: ὡς πρὸς χρεώστην βραδύνοντα τὸν Θεὸν σχετλιάζοντας
problems.why: χρεώστης = creditor/lender, not debtor; God is the one who owes them and is slow to pay.
problems.fix: complaining against God as against a creditor who is slow
problems.ruling: χρεώστης means 'debtor', one who owes; God owes them prosperity, slow to pay. English reverses roles.

problems.quote: whether one is generous and loving toward one another, and whether another is thankful
problems.source_quote: ὁ μὲν, εἰ κοινωνικὸς καὶ φιλάδελφος, ὁ δὲ, εἰ εὐχάριστος
problems.why: English splits one person into two; source contrasts two qualities in same person (generous/loving vs thankful/blasphemous).
problems.fix: whether one is generous and loving toward others, or whether he is thankful and not, on the contrary, blasphemous
problems.ruling: ὁ μὲν...ὁ δὲ contrasts two types of people; 'one...another' correctly renders this, not splitting one person.

fixed: The Greek 'οὐχ ὡς πρὸς Δεσπότην ἀγανακτοῦντα διακειμένους' means they are not indignant as toward a Master; the English 'not disposed to be indignant' inverts the meaning. Changed to 'not indignant as toward a Master'.
